issues.claim: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row (l. 10632; R5-02's D1 text) tests a hand carve against §4.3's crossing rule for ways: its cause is 'a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve … crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it', and its outcome 'the way or channel moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it'. §4.3's rule (l. 5643–5651) needs a clear width of at least 'the way's width + `clearWidthM`', a soffit meeting §2.7 *The clearance* 'for the crossed way', and a crossing within ± `squareDeg` of square. The home of the channel case is §2.7's support step (6) (b) (l. 2596–2599): a channel 'passes beneath where its crossing of the under-deck strip meets no part of the reservation'. §4.11's carve (l. 8238–8243) agrees with (6) (b). V09 §4.20.2 (4) (l. 3023–3025) restates §7.1 ('a carve across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits'). Take a canal carved obliquely under a wide `open` span, touching no support. Under §2.7 and §4.11 it passes beneath. Under §7.1 no span admits it (moving along the deck does not change its angle), so it is cut at the strip's edges (`bend.raised.around`). Two units, two outcomes for one case. This is new this round: round 4's row tested a carve only against an `open` span.
issues.required_change: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row, cause cell: 'a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve meeting a standing raised way's supports, ramps, stairs, feet or a `vault` span's strip, or crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it (§2.7's support step (6) (a)–(b))' → 'a ground `drawWay` or a moved way meeting a standing raised way's supports, ramps, stairs, feet or a `vault` span's strip, or crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it (§2.7's support step (6) (a)), or a hand carve whose channel's crossing of that strip meets a support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span (§2.7's support step (6) (b))'. Outcome cell: 'the way or channel moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it (`bend.raised.underSpan`)' → 'the way moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it, the channel to the nearest crossing that meets none of these (`bend.raised.underSpan`)'; the rest of the cell stands. Second end, V09 §4.20.2 (4): 'and a ground road T4 `road` draws, a way moved or a carve across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, never over a support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span (`bend.raised.underSpan`), a road no span admits going round it (`bend.raised.around`).' → 'and a ground road T4 `road` draws or a way moved across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, and a carve's channel passes beneath where it meets no support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span, else moves along the deck to the nearest crossing that meets none — never over one (`bend.raised.underSpan`); a road no span admits goes round it, and a channel no crossing passes stops at the under-deck strip's edges (`bend.raised.around`).'. V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.underSpan` source cell takes §7.1's new cause and outcome words.

issues.claim: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row, §2.7's support step (6) (b) and §4.11's carve define a hand carve across a standing raised way. Its crossing is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing that passes (`bend.raised.underSpan`). Where none passes, the channel stops at the under-deck strip's edges, 'ending against the ground as against a berm' (`bend.raised.around`). The raised way is held. No bar runs this. T110-2 (5) (l. 18501–18504) runs an epoch growth, an epoch route and two hand roads; T110-2 (1)–(2) run S5a's outer moat at generation; T-V9-52 runs hand roads. A search of every T- row of the base and the twelve volumes finds no carve meeting a raised way, and round 4's text had none either. A build that bridges the canal across a pier's ring, or leaves the carve out, passes every bar. R5-01 grades an untested edge with a defined outcome MAJOR. Repair-r5-determinism's HAND-OFFS flagged it.
issues.required_change: T110-2 (5): after 'and a hand road wider than every `open` span's clear width drawn across one', add '; a hand carve of a canal across a standing viaduct whose drawn crossing meets a support — moved along the deck to the nearest crossing that meets no support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span, the channel passing beneath with no support in water (`bend.raised.underSpan`) — and one wider than the clear width between every two of its supports, stopped at the under-deck strip's edges, both channel ends against the ground as against a berm, every station, key and span unchanged (`bend.raised.around`)'. Second end, V09 T-V9-52: after 'and one wider than every `open` span goes round it, with `bend.raised.around`', add '; a carve across a viaduct passes beneath clear of its piers, with `bend.raised.underSpan`, and one too wide for every gap between its piers stops at the under-deck strip's edges, with `bend.raised.around`'.

issues.claim: This round's D4 text makes §5.3's gate row (l. 9257) read 'the roads leaving each walled stage (on ground part 0 or at a raised gate; …) equal its gate count (§4.2 S3 (7): its N main gates and any harbour gate placed)'. §4.8 *Gates* (l. 7655–7658) counts a raised gate as a main gate only 'where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace … so roads leaving each walled stage, so counted, = its gate count'. But a raised gate also stands where an elevated road is created across a ring: §4.8 l. 7668–7673 says 'at generation … an elevated road or aqueduct at S6's end across any ring; at an epoch V06 §3.19's founding', and §2.7's support step (3) agrees. An elevated road carries no arterial (§4.3 l. 5709–5714: `link`, joining two high wards, terraces, or a citadel and a great temple). Take a CITY whose elevated road joins a high ward inside a ring to one outside it. By §5.3 the elevated road is counted as a road leaving at a raised gate, yet that raised gate is neither one of the N main gates nor a harbour gate. The stage-end S7 check then fails on a lawful map, or builders differ on whether to count it.
issues.required_change: §5.3's gate row, first parenthesis: '(on ground part 0 or at a raised gate; a deck passing over a stretch laid after its raised way is no crossing, §2.7's support step (6) (d))' → '(its arterials, on ground part 0 or at a raised gate where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace, §4.8 *Gates*; a raised gate whose raised way carries no arterial — an elevated road's — and a deck passing over a stretch laid after its raised way are no crossing of this count, §2.7's support step (3), (6) (d))'. The ≥ count's parenthesis stands.

issues.claim: V06 §3.7.2 (1) (l. 1476–1478) opens 'each gate of the ring … → `gateToJunction`' on every ring with a pathway, sparing none. By §4.8 *Gates*, a raised gate is a main gate of the ring, 'a gate whose tower carries the deck, its portal on the raised part only' (l. 7671–7673). §2.7's support step (3) (l. 2556–2565) holds the stretch under a crossing station while the deck stands, and R5-02 says no removal of the wall takes it. Its list of removals that pass over the stretch is: `DeclineOp`'s breach and dismantle, V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay, a hand op's dry run, a delete, `wallToWay`, `absorbWall` and the hand-off down. V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1611–1619) spares the stretch from (2)'s dismantling. Neither names (1)'s gate opening, and `gateToJunction` has only its type (§4.11 l. 8197) and `wallToWay`'s 'gates become junctions'. On V06's ordinary pathway a CITY whose S4 viaduct took a raised gate in S3's ring has that ring superseded, and its gates open by chance each year. A builder can make a junction on the deck (against item 110 (f)'s zero junctions), remove the tower carrying the deck (leaving it unsupported), or skip the gate. The outcome is undefined on a normal path. A hand `convert` `gateToJunction` of a raised gate falls only under §2.7 (3)'s generic 'a hand op's dry run bends its stretch round it', and §7.1's `bend.wall.held` row, which lists the held stretch's removals, does not name it.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.7.2 (1): 'Each gate of the ring, from its drawn' → 'Each gate of the ring — but a raised gate, whose portal on the deck joins no ground way and whose tower carries the deck (§2.7's support step (3); V06 §3.7.6 (5)), which is no candidate, the part-0 way's own ground gate beneath it, if any, a candidate as any gate — from its drawn'. V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s last bullet: after 'V06 §3.7.2 (2)'s dismantling never takes the stretch that holds a raised gate whose deck stands', add ', nor (1)'s gate opening the raised gate'. T-V6-47's H-AQUA clauses add 'a superseded ring whose raised gate carries a standing viaduct's deck — its gates opened over the pathway, the raised gate kept with its tower carrying the deck, no junction on the deck'. Second end, model, §2.7's support step (3): 'and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle` and V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay pass over it in chain order' → 'and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle`, V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay and V06 §3.7.2 (1)'s gate opening (`gateToJunction`, which never takes a raised gate) pass over it in chain order'. Second end, determinism, §7.1's `bend.wall.held` cause: 'a hand `convert` `breach` or `dismantle` of an enceinte stretch' → 'a hand `convert` `breach`, `dismantle` or `gateToJunction` of an enceinte stretch or of its raised gate'.

issues.claim: This round §7.1 (l. 10632) gives `bend.raised.around` both to a way that no span admits (routed round) and to a hand carve's channel that no crossing passes, 'stop[ped] at the under-deck strip's edges'. V09 §4.9's row (l. 2103) words only the way: 'No arch of {way} is wide or high enough for {name}, so it goes round.' Its source cell is 'a ground way no span of a standing raised way admits'. So the dry run's line tells the user that a stopped canal goes round. V09's round-5 HAND-OFF waited for §7.1 to name the key, and §7.1 now has. This is wording only: what is built and tested does not change.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.around` row, words: 'No arch of {way} is wide or high enough for {name}, so it goes round.' → 'No arch of {way} is wide or high enough for {name}, so it goes round.' for a way, and '{name} cannot pass beneath {way} here, so it stops short of it on both sides.' for a channel — the line taking its form by what was drawn, as `{name}` already names a way or a channel. Source cell: add '; and a hand carve's channel that no crossing of the under-deck strip passes, stopped at its edges (§7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row; §2.7's support step (6) (b))'.
